entities.summary:
Theagenes of Rhegium

Theagenes of Rhegium was a Greek literary critic of the 6th century BC from Rhegium, in Magna Graecia. He is best known for being one of the seven scribes of the Septuagint, a Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible, and for his work on the interpretation of Homer's Iliad. Theagenes' critical approach to literature had a significant impact on the development of Greek literary criticism, influencing later scholars such as Aristotle and Longinus.

Theagenes' significance extends to his role in shaping the literary canon of ancient Greece, and his influence can still be seen in modern literary theory and criticism.

This critical approach to literature continues to shape our understanding of the Iliad and the broader corpus of ancient Greek literature.

Theagenes' legacy is a testament to the enduring power of Greek literature to shape our understanding of the world and ourselves.

The Septuagint, which Theagenes helped to translate, played a significant role in the development of Jewish and Christian theology.

Theagenes' work on Homer's Iliad contributed to a deeper understanding of the epic poem's themes and characters.

Theagenes' critical approach to literature had a lasting impact on the development of literary criticism, influencing generations of scholars.
